roles.title: Forest Supervisor
roles.org: USDA Forest Service — a national forest
roles.bio: Line officer for a national forest of a million-plus acres, balancing timber, fire, water, recreation, grazing, and Tribal consultation under federal law, with a thinner staff and more acres burning each decade.

mandates.why: Restoration at scale: heal the landscape, keep the work paying for itself, and protect downstream water, without closing the forest to the public.
Multiple use and public trust: a forest people visit, Congress funds, and downstream users rely on.

ability.name: Line Officer's Decision
ability.text: Once per game: you sign the decision memo. Decide one Dilemma outright, overriding the vote.

future.holding: Forest Supervisor, Still Answering Every Phone

roles.title: Federal Wildland Fire Director
roles.org: Federal wildland fire program (Forest Service or a consolidated federal fire service)
roles.bio: Leads federal wildland fire for a region: suppression, fuels, prescribed fire, aviation, and crews. Whether the program stays in the Forest Service or moves to a unified federal fire agency, the job is safe, effective fire on the land.

mandates.why: Fire-adapted landscapes: fewer destructive fires, a seasoned workforce, and communities ready for the smoke and flames that will still come.
A durable fire organization: stable funding and a career workforce, whatever the org chart says, without losing public trust.

ability.name: Stop the Spread
ability.text: Once per game: initial attack holds. Cancel one negative effect from a System Response cascade as it happens.

roles.title: Forest Service Research Station Director
roles.bio: Directs a research station's scientists, experimental forests, and inventory data. Turns science into tools managers actually use, while protecting decades-long monitoring records through budget swings and reorganizations.

mandates.why: Adaptation science: understand what climate is doing to forests and keep the people and data to act on it.
Science to practice: research embedded with managers, Tribes, and universities, and funded long enough to matter.

ability.name: Horizon Scan
ability.text: Once per game: discard your hand and draw three Signals from the Far horizon.

roles.title: State Forester
roles.bio: Runs the state forestry agency: fire on state and private land, service forestry for family landowners, urban forests, and trust lands. Partners with the Forest Service through Shared Stewardship and answers to a governor and legislature.

mandates.why: Shared stewardship: one plan across ownerships, fewer catastrophic fires, and a forest economy that pays for the work.
Keep forests as forests: healthy woods, safe communities, and steady state authority and funding for both.

ability.name: Forest Action Plan
ability.text: Once per game: bring new options to the table. Replace up to two strategies in the Council market.

roles.title: State Fire & Good Neighbor Program Manager
roles.org: State forestry agency — fire and cross-boundary programs
roles.bio: Manages Good Neighbor agreements and cross-boundary fire programs, putting state crews, contractors, and sale staff to work on federal land and reinvesting receipts in the next restoration project.

mandates.why: Cross-boundary work: crews and agreements that treat whole firesheds, not just one ownership at a time.
A Good Neighbor economy: timber receipts and local contractors fund more restoration, without trading away carbon.

ability.name: Good Neighbor Agreement
ability.text: Once per game: shared crews and receipts cut the cost of one Partnership-tagged strategy by 2.

roles.title: Tribal Natural Resources Director
roles.org: Natural resources department of a sovereign Tribal Nation
roles.bio: Leads natural resources for a sovereign Tribal Nation: forestry, fisheries, cultural fire, first foods, and treaty-reserved rights. Negotiates co-stewardship with federal and state agencies government-to-government, grounded in Indigenous knowledge.

mandates.why: Cultural fire and co-stewardship: Tribal authority on the ground and good fire returned to the land.
Homelands and first foods: healthy forests, clean water, and a stable climate for the generations to come.

ability.name: Cultural Fire Knowledge
ability.text: Once per game: practitioners bring generations of knowledge. +2 to Fire & Fuels, Forest Health, or Partnerships.

roles.title: County Commissioner
roles.org: Board of Commissioners of a forest-dependent county
roles.bio: Elected commissioner of a rural county that is mostly federal land. Balances road, school, and emergency budgets tied to timber receipts and federal payments, and lives with the results of every fire season and mill decision.

mandates.why: A working rural economy: mill jobs, visitors, and a tax base that keeps schools and roads open.
A safe, fire-adapted county: hardened homes, evacuation routes, and reliable federal and state partners to pay for them.

ability.name: Field Hearing
ability.text: Once per game: the county brings the delegation to town. Cancel one negative effect of an Era Driver as it happens.

roles.title: Water Utility General Manager
roles.bio: Runs a water utility serving several hundred thousand people whose drinking water begins on national forest land. Treats post-fire sediment and shrinking snowpack as ratepayer costs, and invests upstream through watershed partnerships.

mandates.why: Source-water security: fewer fires in the watershed and reservoirs that do not fill with ash.
Watershed investment: ratepayer dollars and partners restoring the upper basin as snowpack shifts.

ability.name: Source Water Protection
ability.text: Once per game: the utility stands guard. Protect Water, Forest Health, or Fire & Fuels from Signal effects until the era ends.

roles.title: Mill & Mass Timber Executive
roles.org: Family-owned sawmill and mass timber manufacturer
roles.bio: Operates a family sawmill and a new cross-laminated timber plant. Needs predictable log supply, including small-diameter restoration wood, skilled workers, and building codes and buyers that favor wood.

mandates.why: Mass timber growth: restoration wood becomes buildings that store carbon and keep a mill town working.
Supply certainty: steady federal and state volume, a trained workforce, and a mill that survives the next fire.

ability.name: Order Book
ability.text: Once per game: a signed purchase order de-risks the deal. Reduce the cost of one Wood-tagged strategy by 2.

roles.title: Family Forest Owners Association President
roles.bio: Volunteer president of an association of family woodland owners — retirees, ranchers, heirs — who together own much of the state's forest. Champions technical help, fair markets, fire safety, and keeping land in the family.

mandates.why: Markets for working woodlands: timber and carbon income that make it worth keeping the land as forest.
Fire-safe family forests: woodlots the family still enjoys, and neighbors protected when fire comes over the ridge.

ability.name: Ground Truth
ability.text: Once per game: landowners on the ground say 'not here.' Cancel one negative effect of a Signal as it is played.

roles.title: Conservation Alliance Director
roles.bio: Leads a coalition of conservation groups focused on old forests, wildlife, and climate refugia. Has sued agencies and signed collaborative agreements with them, sometimes the same year, and brings philanthropy and scientists to the table.

mandates.why: Climate refugia: intact, connected forests that store carbon and shelter species, built through collaboration rather than litigation.
Collaboration over conflict: a broad public that loves these forests and partners who restore them together.

ability.name: Philanthropic Match
ability.text: Once per game: a foundation matches the table. Gain 2 extra Capacity in this era's Council.

roles.title: Outdoor Recreation Coalition Director
roles.org: Coalition of outfitters, user groups, and gateway businesses
roles.bio: Speaks for outfitters, trail groups, gateway-town businesses, and millions of visitors. Pushes for maintained trails, fair access, and fees that stay local, and needs open, safe, smoke-free forests to keep the recreation economy running.

mandates.why: Access for all: open trails and staffed sites that welcome everyone and keep gateway towns thriving.
A recreation economy that funds stewardship: rivers, trails, and fee dollars working together.

ability.name: Rally the Public
ability.text: Once per game: public attention shifts. Move up to 2 points from one domain to another.

future.resilient: Experience Concierge for the Public Lands

strategies.title: All-lands fuels treatment
strategies.text: Thin and burn hazardous fuels across federal, state, Tribal, and private land in the firesheds that threaten the most homes and water supplies.

strategies.title: Shared Stewardship compact
strategies.text: State and Forest Service leaders sign joint priorities, share data and staff, and plan treatments together across the whole landscape.

strategies.title: Tribal co-stewardship agreements
strategies.text: Government-to-government agreements give Tribal Nations lasting stewardship roles, co-management where law allows, and fund cultural burning and Indigenous knowledge in planning and monitoring.

strategies.title: Community wildfire defense
strategies.text: Fund community wildfire protection plans, home hardening, defensible space, and evacuation routes in the highest-risk neighborhoods.

strategies.title: Conservation corps pipeline
strategies.text: Paid youth, veteran, and Tribal crews with apprenticeships that lead to permanent agency, contractor, and fire jobs.

strategies.title: Listen-first public engagement
strategies.text: Listening sessions, open project dashboards, and youth programs rebuild trust before the next controversial project or fire season.

strategies.title: Good Neighbor expansion
strategies.text: States, counties, and Tribes do restoration and timber work on national forests, reinvesting receipts into the next project.

strategies.title: Workforce housing partnership
strategies.text: Agencies, counties, and nonprofits build housing so seasonal and permanent staff can afford to live near the forests they manage.

strategies.title: Local restoration contractors
strategies.text: Multi-year stewardship contracts give local logging and restoration businesses the certainty to hire, buy equipment, and stay.

strategies.title: River & trail stewardship partners
strategies.text: Outfitters, user groups, and volunteers adopt trails and river reaches, fixing erosion and reporting problems in exchange for access.

strategies.title: Outdoor access & equity
strategies.text: Shuttles, accessible trails, multilingual programs, and school partnerships bring new and underserved visitors to public lands.

strategies.title: Beaver & meadow restoration
strategies.text: Low-tech, process-based restoration (beaver dam analogs, wet meadows, riparian buffers) stores water, cools streams, and slows fire.

strategies.title: Burn-boss pipeline & liability reform
strategies.text: Training exchanges, state liability standards, and a burn claims fund put more good fire on the ground, at the cost of more smoke days.

strategies.title: Utility watershed investment fund
strategies.text: Water utilities add a ratepayer charge to co-fund thinning, burning, and restoration in the source watersheds they depend on.

strategies.title: Small-wood & biomass markets
strategies.text: Incentives for biochar, pellets, and combined heat and power make thinning small trees pay, though burning biomass adds emissions.

strategies.title: Litigation-resilient planning
strategies.text: Invest in strong analysis, early collaboration, and objection resolution so landscape projects hold up in court, at a real cost in staff time.

strategies.title: Recreation fee reinvestment
strategies.text: Modernize trails and campgrounds, keep fee revenue local, and market gateway towns, bringing more visitors and more wear on fragile sites.

strategies.title: Family forest carbon program
strategies.text: Enroll small landowners in high-integrity carbon programs that pay for deferred harvest and better management, trimming near-term log supply.

strategies.title: Year-round fire workforce
strategies.text: Permanent pay, year-round crews, housing, and mental-health support keep experienced firefighters, but compete for scarce budget dollars.

strategies.title: Accelerated timber output
strategies.text: Raise harvest targets and streamline approvals to boost volume quickly, strengthening mills and county receipts but straining habitat and trail access.

strategies.title: Mature & old-growth safeguards
strategies.text: Durable protection for old and mature stands and roadless areas, paired with active stewardship around them, reducing some timber supply.

strategies.title: Pest early detection & rapid response
strategies.text: Trap networks, detector dogs, and fast strike teams catch invasive insects and diseases early; quarantines restrict log and firewood movement.

strategies.title: Post-fire recovery strike teams
strategies.text: Interagency teams stabilize burned slopes, warn downstream towns of debris flows, and replant with utility and Tribal partners.

strategies.title: Lean operations consolidation
strategies.text: Close or merge offices and shift functions to regional hubs, saving money fast but thinning local staff and visitor services.

strategies.title: Nursery & reforestation surge
strategies.text: Expand seed collection, nurseries, and planting crews to close the post-fire reforestation backlog with climate-informed stock.

strategies.title: AI & remote-sensing early warning
strategies.text: Satellites, cameras, and drones with machine-learning detection flag new ignitions, beetle kill, and drought stress early, and share the data openly.

strategies.title: Seed banks & assisted migration
strategies.text: Bank genetically diverse seed, test climate-adapted sources in trial plantings, and update seed-zone rules for a warmer future.

strategies.title: Science-to-practice partnerships
strategies.text: Research stations, universities, and extension embed scientists with managers to co-design treatments and monitor what works.

strategies.title: Working-forest conservation finance
strategies.text: Blend Forest Legacy, state, philanthropic, and private capital into easements that keep family and industrial forests working and intact.

strategies.title: Climate-ready forest plans
strategies.text: Revise land management plans around climate scenarios, drought refugia, and carbon, accepting slower project approvals while plans change.

strategies.title: Mass timber procurement standard
strategies.text: Public buildings specify mass timber made from restoration wood, giving mills a steady buyer and storing carbon in schools and housing.

strategies.title: Stable fire & land budgets
strategies.text: A broad coalition wins predictable multi-year funding so suppression costs stop draining fuels, research, and recreation programs.

strategies.title: WUI land-use & insurance compact
strategies.text: State codes, county zoning, and insurer discounts reward fire-adapted development: a hard political lift with lasting payoff.

strategies.title: Unified federal fire service
strategies.text: Consolidate federal wildland fire into one agency with common standards and careers: promising efficiency, risking disruption to shared crews and land-management ties.

strategies.title: Forest resilience bond
strategies.text: Private investors front the cost of restoration; utilities, agencies, and insurers repay them as avoided-fire benefits arrive.

cascades.text: A growing fire deficit: big fires keep burning through source watersheds and into towns.
Heat and drought outrun adaptation: drought stress and beetles keep killing trees.
Dead and dying stands become fuel and turn from carbon sink to source.
Ash-choked reservoirs and drying streams hit towns and riparian forests.
The last mill closes; loggers and the restoration workforce leave with it.
Rural distress and insurance retreat erode the tax base and the public's patience.
No one left to staff crews or keep agreements alive.
Trust collapses into lawsuits and go-it-alone projects.
A united coalition makes the budget case together and wins.
A timber boom pays wages and county bills, and pulls harvest toward older stands.
Record crowds create new champions for the forest, and new wear on fragile places.
Thriving towns sprawl deeper into fire country: more homes and ignitions to defend.
